key_insight: The paper shows that measurement-free surface-code state preparation can be improved by using digital-analog counterdiabatic controls that approximate the needed four-body stabilizer dynamics with native superconducting operations.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to lower-depth logical-state initialization on near-term superconducting hardware, which is critical for scalable quantum error correction.
method: Builds a variational adiabatic gauge potential ansatz from stabilizer-local counterdiabatic terms.
Maps the resulting operators to digital-analog blocks using fixed-angle XY gates, single-qubit rotations, and analog exchange evolution.
Applies the construction to checkerboard plaquette-stabilizer lattices up to 4x4 and generalizes it to n x m grids.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmarking on checkerboard grids up to 4x4, with improved short-time ground-state preparation over bare adiabatic evolution and up to an order-of-magnitude reduction in entangling depth.
watch_item: The approach relies on accurate control of digital-analog blocks and may be sensitive to hardware imperfections when scaling to larger lattices.
paper_title: Measurement-free Preparation of Surface-Code States with Digital-Analog Counterdiabatic Drivings
